## What the statements say, for ffms2
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch ffms2
    ./oft verify-sha ffms2

By hand: download `ffms2-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.10.0](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0), unpack it into `projects/ffms2/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; an OSS-Fuzz testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [FFMS/ffms2](https://github.com/FFMS/ffms2) at `3af2ef2ae47bc30b64597c9e419e5b19c4bda7d8`, built with autotools
- Harnesses: the harness files are modified in `ffms2_fuzzer` (see each harness page)
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. A binary whose SHA-256 differs after a rebuild with it is a bug: please open an issue.

## Licence
ffms2 is under `MIT`. Each binary is a combined work of ffms2, the harness, the C library, the compiler's runtime and every library it links; the SPDX expression of each is not recorded here yet. Corresponding source, in release [v2026.10.0-src](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0-src): `ffms2-src.tar.zst`, the upstream source trees exactly as upstream publishes them; `ffms2-src.MANIFEST.tsv`, which says where the build lays each one down; and `recipe.tar.zst`, that release's build recipe (the build scripts, pins and patches). Its binaries are under a GPL-family licence, so their corresponding source also takes `toolchain-src.tar.zst`, the source of the toolchain they were built with, and `sysroot-src.tar.zst`, the source of every library they link from the build image, in release [sources-v1](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/sources-v1).
